text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor

The pain you describe when eating is highly suggestive of trigeminal nerve irritation; are you experiencing any numbness, tingling, or altered sensation in your chin, upper lip, or tongue? Additionally, have you noticed any discharge, bleeding, or visible swelling behind your right ear when wearing earrings?

speaker: Doctor

DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Granulomatous Mastoiditis (CGM) with Trigeminal Neuralgia secondary to prior tympanoplasty.

The combination of shooting pain triggered by mastication and tenderness over the ear canal, despite normal CT and ABR results, strongly suggests an infectious granuloma mimicking nerve compression. Have you noticed any localized redness, warmth, or a small, painless lump behind your right ear?
